gently: Please pat the tiny bunny gently, as its fur is so soft.
Turn the thin old pages gently so they do not tear.
The breeze blew gently, and the leaves barely moved.
quickly: The bus is about to leave, so we must run quickly!
She quickly ate her toast because the bell was about to ring.
Hurry up and get dressed quickly, or we will miss the bus.
happily: The story ended with everyone living happily ever after.
With a glad heart, he sat happily by the window.
How happily we waved, glad that the holiday had begun!
easily: It is so light that I can easily carry it!
Can you reach the top shelf easily or do you need steps?
The tall girl could easily see over the fence.
noisily: The lorry rumbled noisily down our street and woke the baby.
Why is the washing machine rattling so noisily today?
Don't eat your crisps so noisily in the quiet library!
angrily: My dad was cross about the muddy floor and frowned angrily.
She glared angrily at the broken kite and folded her arms.
Cross about the lost game, he sat angrily with his arms folded.
basically: A pancake is basically flour, eggs and milk.
The cake is basically done, so we just need the icing.
The two paintings are basically the same, but one has more blue.
magically: In the story, the pumpkin magically became a golden coach.
The old teapot magically turned into a tiny silver bird.
Did the cards magically float up from the table?
fantastically: Our class did fantastically in the spelling test!
My kite flew fantastically well, and we cheered in the park.
We had a fantastically good time at the seaside today.
dramatically: She flopped dramatically onto the sofa, like an actor in a play.
With a grand sweep of his arm, the dancer bowed dramatically.
He pointed dramatically at the cake, like an actor on a stage.

rejected.s: How gently Dad rocked the little baby to sleep!

rejected.s: Quickly, the cat dashed up the tree after the fluttering leaf.
rejected.reason: checker: Dashed already shows speed, so dramatically or happily could also start the sentence. (also fits: dramatically, happily)

rejected.s: The fast cyclist went by so quickly that I blinked.
rejected.reason: checker: Saying that I blinked is an odd result of something going fast, so the sentence reads unnaturally.

rejected.s: Her sandcastle was fantastically tall, with towers and a flag.
rejected.reason: reader flag two_fit ('dramatically' also fits: 'Her sandcastle was dramatically tall' makes sense too.); re-judge: The flag is real. 'Dramatically' can describe an adjective to mean 'strikingly', so 'dramatically tall' is acceptable English, and 'magically tall' could also work. More than one bank word fits, so drop this sentence.
